key_idea: Shows the projection of a cube onto the y-z plane

blocks.name: Setup
blocks.description: The initial spatial context, including the object and coordinate system.

elements.enriched_role: The 3D object being transformed; it is aligned with the coordinate axes.
Establish the 3D coordinate system (x, y, z) and orientation in space.

blocks.name: Mechanism
blocks.description: A projection operation that maps the cube onto the yz-plane.

elements.enriched_role: Arrows map vertices on cube to vertices onto the projected shape, emphasising the operation is vertex by vertex and not the cube as a whole, and therefore is likely a projection rather than, say, a translation. The projection is orthogonal.

refinements: The projection is orthogonal (projection lines are perpendicular to the yz-plane, i.e. parallel to the x-axis), so the x-dimension is simply dropped.

blocks.name: Result
blocks.description: The result of the projection of the cube is a square on the yz-plane.

elements.element: shaded square on the y-z plane
elements.current_role: the resultant shape of the projection
elements.enriched_role: The result of the projection, it is placed on the yz-plane and occupies the same yz coordinates as the cube.

key_idea: Demonstrates the folding of a cube net, using two labels to keep track of its orientation

blocks.name: Setup
blocks.description: The flat template and reference markers before any transformation.

elements.enriched_role: The 2D cross/t-shaped arrangement of 6 connected square faces representing an unfolded cube.
A distinct square marker placed on one face to track spatial position during folding.
An oriented marker that tracks both spatial position and directional orientation (facing/rotation) across the transformation.

blocks.name: Mechanism
blocks.description: The transformation connecting the flat and assembled forms.

elements.element: arrow from net to folded cube
elements.enriched_role: Represents the dynamic process of folding 2D faces along edges into a 3D box shape.

blocks.name: Result
blocks.description: The assembled 3D form showing where the reference markers end up.

elements.current_role: depiction of the net after folding, with the labels tracking the orientation of the cube
elements.enriched_role: The assembled 3D cube showing the final relative positions and orientations of the square and arrow reference markers.

key_idea: Rays can intersect a circle at zero, one, or two points.

blocks.name: Setup
blocks.description: The geometric primitives involved in the intersection test.

elements.enriched_role: Three linear trajectory paths representing test rays at varying distances from the circle center.
The 2D circular boundary being tested for ray intersection.

blocks.name: Mechanism
blocks.description: The spatial relationship between the line and the curved boundary.

elements.enriched_role: The geometric traversal of rays relative to the circle (outside/miss, tangent/touch, secant/penetrate).

blocks.name: Result
blocks.description: The points where contact occurs, varying by case.

elements.current_role: 0, 1, or 2 points depending on the case
elements.enriched_role: The discrete contact count (0 points for miss, 1 point for tangent, 2 points for secant) highlighting intersection count variation.

key_idea: The effect of moving the observer away from the view plane is that the field/angle of view narrows or, put differently, the scene becomes more zoomed in

blocks.name: Setup
blocks.description: The scene and the fixed constraint through which it is viewed.

elements.enriched_role: A generic 3D target scene object positioned at a fixed location.
A fixed rectangular aperture/window defining the spatial framing constraint.

blocks.name: Mechanism
blocks.description: The change in observer position relative to the viewing constraint.

elements.current_role: depicts the observer moving away from the view plane, from an initial to secondary position
elements.enriched_role: The backward displacement of the camera/viewpoint relative to the static view plane.
Indicates direction of viewpoint translation (moving further away).

elements.current_role: shows the view of the observer through the view plane from each of the initial and secondary positions
elements.enriched_role: Frustum rays passing from observer through view plane boundaries onto the scene.

blocks.name: Result
blocks.description: The observable change in how much of the scene is visible.

elements.enriched_role: The reduced angular field of view resulting in a zoomed-in perspective of the target object.

key_idea: a shadow ray from a point not in shadow to the light source does not intersect any objects, while one from a point in shadow does intersect an object

blocks.name: Setup
blocks.description: The light source, occluding object, and test points in the scene.

elements.enriched_role: Point light emitting illumination rays across the scene.
Opaque obstacle obstructing light ray paths.
Surface sample positions evaluated for light visibility.

blocks.name: Mechanism
blocks.description: Tracing paths from each test point toward the light source to check for obstruction.

elements.current_role: rays from p1/p2 to light source and check if intersection with circle
elements.enriched_role: Raycasting straight lines from surface points back to light source position to query ray-geometry intersection.

blocks.name: Result
blocks.description: Whether each path is blocked determines if the point is in shadow.

elements.current_role: if the shadow-ray intersects the circle/an obstacle, the point casting that ray is in shadow. Otherwise, it is not
elements.enriched_role: Existence of an intersection hit along p2's shadow ray flags p2 as occluded/shadowed, whereas p1's unobstructed ray leaves p1 illuminated.

key_idea: the distance from a point to a plane can be computed by finding the magnitude of the projection of the vector from the origin to the point onto the plane's normal, and comparing it with the distance of the plane to the origin along that normal

blocks.name: Setup
blocks.description: The geometric primitives: the plane, the point, and the reference direction.

elements.enriched_role: Target 3D plane specified in implicit or point-normal form.
Arbitrary 3D point location to measure distance from plane.
Perpendicular unit vector defining the plane's orientation axis.

blocks.name: Mechanism
blocks.description: Using the reference direction to decompose the point's position and compute a perpendicular measurement.

elements.current_role: projecting origin-to-p vector onto normal vector
elements.enriched_role: Dot product projection of point vector onto normal n to measure scalar distance along normal direction.

elements.element: orthogonal distance from origin to p
elements.current_role: can compare/subtract the lengths of this vector with/from the projection vector to obtain the result d
elements.enriched_role: Comparing projected point distance against plane offset distance d' along normal n to isolate point-to-plane distance d.

blocks.name: Result
blocks.description: The computed perpendicular distance from the point to the plane.

elements.enriched_role: The resultant perpendicular offset d between point p and the plane surface.

key_idea: in a ray intersecting the csg object, the ray intersects the box before it leaves the circle, and in a ray not intersecting the csg object, the ray leaves the circle before entering the box

blocks.name: Setup
blocks.description: The primitive shapes and their overlapping region.

elements.current_role: primary components of a csg object
elements.enriched_role: Base solid geometries (primitive A and B).

elements.element: intersection area of box and circle
elements.enriched_role: Constructive Solid Geometry boolean intersection region (A ∩ B).

blocks.name: Mechanism
blocks.description: Tracing paths through the primitives and recording the sequence of boundary crossings.

elements.current_role: both pass through the box and circle, but r1 passes through the intersection/csg object while r2 does not
elements.enriched_role: Test rays traversing primitives, generating entry/exit interval spans.

elements.element: ordered list of intersection points for each ray
elements.current_role: lists the order of intersection points for each ray with each primitive component by intersection order
elements.enriched_role: Sorted 1D list of interval entry/exit boundary hit points along ray path.

blocks.name: Result
blocks.description: Comparing crossing sequences reveals whether each path passes through the overlap region.

elements.current_role: shows how list order is necessarily different for rays intersecting the csg object and those not, or something similar
elements.enriched_role: Evaluating boolean interval overlap: r1 shows entry into box before exiting circle (valid hit in A ∩ B), whereas r2 exits circle before entering box (no hit).

key_idea: Demonstrates a composite affine transformation: an arrow is rotated 90 degrees from the z-axis to the y-axis, then scaled up by a factor of 2.

blocks.name: Setup
blocks.description: A 3D coordinate frame (x, y, z) with an initial unit arrow lying along the z-axis.

elements.current_role: provides spatial orientation and tick marks measuring scale
elements.enriched_role: Establishes 3D spatial orientation and scale markings (ticks at 1, 2, etc.).

elements.current_role: the starting 3D object before transformation, pointing along the z-axis
elements.enriched_role: The starting geometry positioned at the origin and oriented forward along the z-axis.

refinements: The initial arrow has unit height (reaches tick 1).

blocks.name: Mechanism
blocks.description: A sequential two-step affine transformation: a 90-degree rotation followed by scaling.

elements.current_role: indicates a 90-degree rotation of the arrow from the z-axis to the y-axis
elements.enriched_role: Indicates rotation of the arrow from the z-axis up to the y-axis (around the x-axis).

elements.current_role: indicates scaling the upright arrow by a factor of 2 along the coordinate axes
elements.enriched_role: Indicate scaling along the coordinate axes.

refinements: Identifies rotation as 90 degrees around the x-axis.
Identifies scaling as uniform / by a factor of 2.
Identifies the sequence: rotation occurs first, then scaling.

blocks.name: Result
blocks.description: The final arrow stands upright along the y-axis with doubled dimensions (height of 2 and doubled width).

elements.current_role: the final transformed object, standing along the y-axis with doubled dimensions
elements.enriched_role: The transformed object reaching y=2 with doubled width.

refinements: The final arrow has height 2 and doubled width compared to the original.
